source: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) & National Institutes of Health (NIH)
document_title: Defining Adult Overweight & Obesity; Clinical Guidelines on the Identification, Evaluation, and Treatment of Overweight and Obesity in Adults
guideline_statement: A BMI of 18.5 to 24.9 kg/m² falls within the healthy weight range for adults. A BMI of 25.0 to 29.9 kg/m² falls within the overweight range. A BMI of 30.0 kg/m² or higher falls within the obesity range. Elevated BMI is a major contributing factor to peripheral insulin resistance.
clinical_context: BMI is an anthropometric screening indicator, not a direct measure of body adiposity distribution or visceral fat. Clinical evaluation should consider waist circumference and muscle mass.

source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)
guideline_statement: Normal fasting serum insulin generally ranges from 2 to 25 mu U/ml, while 2-hour postprandial insulin typically remains under 166 mu U/ml. Elevated circulating insulin in the setting of normal or elevated glucose suggests compensatory hyperinsulinemia secondary to cellular insulin resistance.
clinical_context: Insulin levels fluctuate rapidly based on assay methodology, recent carbohydrate intake, and hepatic clearance. Serum insulin tests are primarily utilized in research and specialized metabolic assessments rather than routine first-line diabetes screening.

source: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)
document_title: Pima Indians Diabetes Clinical Research Archive
section: Anthropometric and Hereditary Features in Type 2 Diabetes Studies

reference_ranges.pedigree_score_median: 0.372 (Pima study sample median; higher values indicate stronger familial clustering)

clinical_context: A higher pedigree score denotes stronger familial clustering of diabetes. Family history is a non-modifiable risk indicator that lowers the threshold for routine clinical metabolic screening.
